prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the bus occupies most of the space directly ahead and shifts from left/front at roughly 1–3 m to extremely close on the left and center, with its doorway and driver area about 0.5–1.5 m away by the final frames. A bicycle-like object stays low near the bus’s right-front edge at about 1–2 m, while a car and background trees, road, and sidewalk remain several metres farther away; the driver is inside the bus, behind the windshield and above the bicycle. The bright near-field regions clarify the bus’s large foreground extent, its occlusion of the background, and the camera wearer’s approach and rightward turn toward the doorway, which are less explicit in RGB alone. Metric distances are only rough because the map supplies relative depth, and it appears unreliable around reflective windows, thin bicycle parts, frame boundaries, and the final-frame foreground bag or clothing.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks isolate a bus dominating the left and central foreground in frames 1–3, people at the bus edge or inside it, a bicycle low on the right, and a small car farther right; in frames 4–5, a nearby seated person is above and behind two close rectangular objects on the right side. The bus grows from roughly 2–4 m away to about 0.5–1.5 m and progressively blocks the sidewalk and background, while the bicycle remains about 1–2 m away and partly cropped or occluded near the lower edge. The map makes object boundaries, overlap, and left/right relationships clearer than RGB, especially where dark windows hide the person inside, but it provides no direct metric depth or facing direction. Several labels and masks are unreliable: the close objects marked “laptop” and “tv” do not align convincingly with the RGB scene, some people are reduced to tiny fragments, bus masks change colour across frames, and many visible structures are omitted.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it supplies no body or hand keypoints and therefore cannot establish limb locations, facing direction, gaze toward the camera wearer, reach, or person-to-person spacing. From this map alone, no people or objects can be placed, no occlusions can be resolved, and no approach, retreat, or turning can be tracked across time. Relative to the RGB strip, it reveals no additional spatial structure and is unreliable here because the pose detector appears to have failed or produced no detections, likely leaving even the visible driver and other person unrepresented.
